readiness.summary: This app needs changes before Deployz can deploy it.

findings.title: Relies on its own message queue
findings.whyItMatters: Deployz provisions one container per application with managed database, cache, and storage. Extra infrastructure the app expects would not exist at runtime.
findings.suggestedOutcome: Keep the queue code. Deploy on Deployz only if the app can use a queue Deployz provides (Redis or Amazon SQS), or if the queue dependency is not actually used.
findings.technicalEvidence: Unsupported infrastructure: docker-compose.yaml requires a Temporal server (service "temporal", image temporalio/auto-setup:1.28.1) which Deployz does not provision.
findings.plainEnglishExplanation: This app depends on a message queue or event bus that Deployz does not host (for example Kafka, RabbitMQ, or an AWS queue).

findings.title: Give Deployz a way to update your database
findings.whyItMatters: Deployz runs your migration command automatically on every deploy, so each customer database always matches the code that talks to it.
findings.suggestedOutcome: If the app already updates its database when it starts, change nothing. Otherwise set a command that applies the migrations non-interactively in the application settings.
findings.technicalEvidence: A PostgreSQL library is present (@prisma/client) but no migration command was found in the image start path or any package.json.
findings.plainEnglishExplanation: This app uses a database, but Deployz could not find a command that updates the database structure during deploys.

findings.title: Background job runner
findings.whyItMatters: Deployz runs each declared worker as its own process. Jobs that need a separate runner do not run until one is declared.
findings.suggestedOutcome: If the web process already runs the jobs, change nothing. Otherwise declare the job runner with its own start command (for example a Procfile worker line).
findings.plainEnglishExplanation: This app appears to run background jobs, but no command exists that starts a job runner as a separate process.
